## Mechanism

**Palm — near-term loose, longer-term right-tailed.** Malaysian closing stocks of 2.82 MMT [N61] with 2.18 months of export cover [N8] are the loosening leg: rising month-end inventory works against price with a zero-to-one-quarter lag, high confidence. Against it sits the largest reading on this estate — the dry-day run over the SE Asian palm belt at 1.25 z [N13], 97th percentile [N15], rising three months — which the model moves in the same direction as palm price with a two-to-four-quarter lag, high confidence, plus the warm-phase Pacific reading of +1.8 degC [N16], also same-direction on palm at high confidence. That is where palm's response turns convex: the loose stocks are today's fact, the yield loss is a lagged, biologically irreversible one, and thin export cover is the buffer that would let it tip.

**Rapeseed — loosening, and more of it.** Four of the seven conditions in the model's glut-with-demand-loss pattern read here: EU stocks-to-use at 9.42% [N40] (past the desk's ample line), Ukraine production 4.35 MMT [N31], Australia 7.8 MMT [N37], Canada 22.5 MMT [N34] — the model records Black Sea and Australian abundance as amplifying each other into the EU import book. Offsetting, not overturning: EU crush at 25.4 MMT [N28], 95th percentile [N30], is same-direction support.

**The linkage.** Palm sets the floor of the vegetable-oil complex and pulls rapeseed oil with it; canola and rapeseed are one substitution pair. So a lagged palm supply squeeze is the channel that would lift MATIF against its own loose sheet — which is why the pair reads palm-favoured on a two-to-four-quarter view even while palm's nearby stocks are heavy.

- Boards: MATIF rapeseed November 2026 settled 536.5 EUR/t on 28 September 2026 [N67], the 16th percentile of that contract's own sessions since 6 August 2026 [N71], though up 3.5 EUR/t over twenty-one sessions [N70]. CME palm oil October 2026 settled 1,181 USD/metric ton on 24 September 2026 [N72], the 60th percentile of its own sessions [N77], up 53.5 USD/metric ton over sixty-three sessions [N76] but down 67.5 over twenty-one [N75]. The two settle in different currencies, so no cross-board price comparison is made here.

In March 2026 the USDA attaché wrote that higher 2024/25 palm prices came from Malaysian and Indonesian biodiesel mandates, shifting demand toward more affordable oils [E15] — mechanism for the diversion channel, not a current reading.

## Where the record disagrees

Within palm itself the record points both ways at once, and not by era: stocks at the 94th percentile [N62] settle a lower price on a zero-to-one-quarter clock, while the severe drought reading [N13] settles a higher one on a two-to-four-quarter clock. Same market, different horizons — the near leg is loose, the far leg right-tailed. The counts say seven readings toward a lower palm price against three higher; I lean to the loose nearby read for now and to the drought leg as the horizon extends, because the drought reading is the furthest-out figure on this estate and its run has not turned.

- **EU rapeseed stocks-to-use** [N40], 9.42% for 2026/27, known 11 September 2026: seventeen declared upstream paths land on MATIF price through this one reading, so it is the single confirming figure for the loosening lean. - **The warm-phase Pacific reading** [N16], +1.8 degC, July 2026, eight months rising and past the strong line: it is declared on thirty-four other markets, so a turn here reprices the whole complex, not just these two; its window on MATIF runs 31 October 2026 to 30 April 2027. Wrong if the next print, between 1 and 5 October 2026, returns it to the middle of its own record.
